1/**
2 * \file Log.cpp
3 * \brief Implements the asynchronous application logging system.
4 *
5 * \details
6 * This translation unit installs the Qt message handler, captures and normalizes
7 * message context, formats normal and important log records, manages file and
8 * display worker threads, controls permanent and temporary consoles, persists
9 * runtime configuration, performs log-directory cleanup, and installs fatal and
10 * crash handlers. Important records are forwarded to the external npiImpLog
11 * helper process so that critical information can still be written during fatal
12 * failures and abnormal termination.
13 *
14 * The implementation is Windows-specific and intentionally keeps its central
15 * state alive until process termination so that logging remains available during
16 * static destruction and emergency handling.
17 *
18 * \note
19 * This implementation is intentionally documented selectively. Because the file is
20 * large, comments focus on architecture, ownership, synchronization, invariants,
21 * failure handling, and other non-obvious design decisions. Straightforward code is
22 * generally left uncommented to avoid obscuring the implementation with comments
23 * that merely repeat what the code already expresses.
24 */

184 /**
185 * \brief Identifies a field that can be included in formatted log output.
186 * \details
187 * Values must remain contiguous because field names are reflected with
188 * `magic_enum` and packed into four-bit slots by the layout subsystem.
189 */
190 enum class Field : std::uint8_t {
191 DateTime = 0,
192 Sequence = 1,
193 Level = 2,
194 ThreadIndex = 3,
195 ThreadId = 4,
196 AppTime = 5,
197 ThreadTime = 6,
198 ThreadDelta = 7,
199 Category = 8,
200 FileLine = 9,
201 Function = 10
202 };
203
204 static_assert(magic_enum::enum_count<Field>() == 11u, "Log Fields must be exactly 11");

206 /**
207 * \brief Stores one captured log record for asynchronous processing.
208 * \details
209 * The structure contains compact indices into immutable context caches together
210 * with timestamps, thread information, sequence information, level, and message
211 * text. Its fixed 64-byte layout keeps queue storage predictable.
212 */
213 struct OneLog {
214 // 1 byte fields
215 std::uint8_t level_{1}; ///< Compact Qt level: 0 Debug, 1 Info, 2 Warning, 3 Critical, 4 Fatal.
216 std::uint8_t category_{0}; ///< Category slot obtained from CategoryCache.
217
218 // 2 byte fields
219 std::uint16_t threadIdx_{0};
220 ///< Thread Index, shown as "T#.....", main thread is "T#.MAIN", index 0 is formatted as "T#.????".
221 std::uint16_t fileLine_{0}; ///< File line slot obtained from FileLineCache.
222 std::uint16_t function_{0}; ///< Function slot obtained from FunctionCache.
223
224 // 4 byte fields
225 DWORD threadId_{0}; ///< Windows thread ID obtained using `::GetCurrentThreadId()`, show as "0x...".
226 std::uint32_t sequence_{0}; ///< Wrapping 32-bit sequence number assigned at log capture time.
227 std::uint32_t appTimeMs_{0};
228 ///< Elapsed time since logging-system initialization with millisecond precision, shown as "A=...".
229 std::uint32_t threadTimeMs_{0}; ///< Thread time since it first logged with millisecond precision, shown as "T=...".
230
231 // 8 byte fields
232 std::int64_t threadDeltaNs_{-1};
233 ///< Per-thread log delta in nanoseconds; formatted using adaptive units, shown as "d=...".
234 std::chrono::system_clock::time_point dateTime_{nullDateTime};
235 ///< Wall-clock date and time obtained from the system clock.
236
237 // 24 byte field
238 QString message_; ///< Captured message text.
239
240 /// \brief Converts a Qt message type to the compact internal level value.
241 static std::uint8_t LevelCast_(QtMsgType lvl) noexcept
242 {
243 switch (lvl) {
244 case QtDebugMsg: return 0;
245 case QtInfoMsg: return 1;
246 case QtWarningMsg: return 2;
247 case QtCriticalMsg: return 3;
248 case QtFatalMsg: return 4;
249 }
250 return 1; // Return QtInfoMsg as default
251 }
252 };

257 /**
258 * \brief Provides a fixed-capacity, allocation-free text buffer.
259 *
260 * \details
261 * Text is sanitized as it is appended, whitespace is normalized, the pipe
262 * character is reserved for field separation, and non-ASCII text is represented
263 * with question marks. Multiple fixed-size lines can be accumulated without
264 * dynamic allocation, which also makes the buffer suitable for fatal and crash
265 * paths.
266 *
267 * \tparam LineSize Maximum bytes available to one line, including its terminator.
268 * \tparam LineCount Capacity multiplier; total storage is `LineSize * LineCount`.
269 */
270 template <size_t LineSize, size_t LineCount = 1u>
271 class TextBuffer final {
272 public:
273 static_assert(LineSize >= 128u, "LineSize must be at least 128"); // Minimum line size
274 static_assert(LineCount >= 1u); // Minimum line count
275 static_assert(LineCount <= std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max() / LineSize,
276 "LineSize * LineCount must be within range");
277
278 // Each template instantiation gets its own constant
279 static constexpr size_t LineSize_ = LineSize; ///< Line Size of this template instantiation
280 static constexpr size_t LineCount_ = LineCount; ///< Line Count of this template instantiation
281 static constexpr size_t Capacity_ = LineSize * LineCount;
282 ///< Total capacity in bytes for this template instantiation
283
284 /// \brief Constructs an empty buffer.
285 TextBuffer() noexcept { clear_(); }
286
287 /// \brief Resets the buffer to its first empty line.
288 void clear_() noexcept
289 {
290 pos_ = 0;
291 beg_ = 0;
292 end_ = LineSize_; // The line can contain at most LineSize - 1 payload bytes.
293 buf_[0] = '\0';
294 }
295
296 /// \brief Returns the beginning of the accumulated byte buffer.
297 const char* data_() const noexcept { return buf_; }
298
299 /// \brief Returns the number of accumulated bytes.
300 size_t size_() const noexcept { return pos_; }
301
302 /// \brief Checks whether the buffer contains no accumulated bytes.
303 bool empty_() const noexcept { return pos_ == 0u; }
304
305 /// \brief Checks whether the current line has room for the requested bytes and its terminator.
306 bool canAppend_(size_t len) const noexcept
307 {
308 return pos_ < end_ && end_ - pos_ > len;
309 }
310
311 /// \brief Appends one byte without sanitization.
312 bool appendRawChar_(char chr) noexcept
313 {
314 if (!canAppend_(1u)) return false;
315 buf_[pos_++] = chr;
316 return true;
317 }
318
319 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends one character.
320 bool appendChar_(char chr) noexcept
321 {
322 // UTF-8 encodes non-ASCII Unicode characters using two to four bytes, all above
323 // 127. Since this function sanitizes one byte at a time, one Unicode character
324 // may therefore appear as "??", "???", or "????".
325
326 const auto uChr = static_cast<unsigned char>(chr);
327
328 // Multiple consecutive whitespaces are collapsed into one space.
329 // Space is only added if not at the beginning of the line.
330 if (chr == ' ' || chr == '\t' || chr == '\r' || chr == '\n' || chr == '\v' || chr == '\f') {
331 if (pos_ > beg_ && buf_[pos_ - 1] != ' ' && buf_[pos_ - 1] != '\n') {
332 if (!canAppend_(1u)) return false;
333 buf_[pos_++] = ' ';
334 }
335 return true;
336 }
337
338 if (!canAppend_(1u)) return false;
339 if (chr == '|') buf_[pos_++] = '/'; // replace | with / since | is designated as delimiter for log file.
340 else if (uChr >= 32u && uChr <= 126u) buf_[pos_++] = chr;
341 else buf_[pos_++] = '?';
342 return true;
343 }
344
345 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends one character.
346 bool appendChar_(wchar_t chr) noexcept
347 {
348 // ReSharper disable once CppUnsignedZeroComparison
349 if (chr >= 0 && chr <= 126)
350 return appendChar_(static_cast<char>(chr));
351 return appendRawChar_('?');
352 }
353
354 /// \brief Appends the configured field separator when the current line is not empty.
355 /// \param pipeSep `true` to append `" | "`; `false` to append one separating space.
356 bool appendDelimiter_(bool pipeSep) noexcept
357 {
358 // In case pipeSep is false i.e. for display, we use single space as delimiter.
359
360 if (pos_ == beg_) return true;
361
362 const bool needSpace = buf_[pos_ - 1u] != ' ';
363
364 if (pipeSep) {
365 const size_t len = needSpace ? 3u : 2u;
366 if (!canAppend_(len)) return false;
367 if (needSpace) buf_[pos_++] = ' ';
368 buf_[pos_++] = '|';
369 buf_[pos_++] = ' ';
370 return true;
371 }
372
373 if (!needSpace) return true;
374 return appendRawChar_(' ');
375 }
376
377 /// \brief Appends a bounded byte sequence without sanitization.
378 bool appendRawText_(const char* txt, size_t len) noexcept
379 {
380 if (txt == nullptr || len == 0u) return true;
381 if (!canAppend_(len)) return false;
382 for (size_t ii = 0u; ii < len; ++ii)
383 buf_[pos_++] = txt[ii];
384 return true;
385 }
386
387 /// \brief Appends a bounded byte sequence without sanitization.
388 template <size_t Len>
389 bool appendRawText_(const char (&txt)[Len]) noexcept
390 {
391 // Len cannot be 0 here, at minimum it will be 1
392 return appendRawText_(txt, Len - 1u);
393 }
394
395 /// \brief Copies a bounded byte sequence without per-byte processing.
396 bool appendRawTextFast_(const char* txt, size_t len) noexcept
397 {
398 if (txt == nullptr || len == 0u) return true;
399 if (!canAppend_(len)) return false;
400 std::memcpy(buf_ + pos_, txt, len);
401 pos_ += len;
402 return true;
403 }
404
405 /// \brief Copies a bounded byte sequence without per-byte processing.
406 template <size_t Len>
407 bool appendRawTextFast_(const char (&txt)[Len]) noexcept
408 {
409 // Len cannot be 0 here, at minimum it will be 1
410 return appendRawTextFast_(txt, Len - 1u);
411 }
412
413 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends bounded null-terminated narrow text.
414 bool appendText_(const char* txt, size_t maxScan = 4096u) noexcept
415 {
416 if (txt == nullptr) return true;
417 for (size_t ii = 0u; ii < maxScan && txt[ii] != '\0'; ++ii) {
418 if (!appendChar_(txt[ii])) return false;
419 }
420 return true;
421 }
422
423 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends bounded null-terminated wide text.
424 bool appendText_(const wchar_t* txt, size_t maxScan = 4096u) noexcept
425 {
426 if (txt == nullptr) return true;
427 for (size_t ii = 0u; ii < maxScan && txt[ii] != L'\0'; ++ii) {
428 if (!appendChar_(txt[ii])) return false;
429 }
430 return true;
431 }
432
433 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends a `QStringView` without allocation.
434 /// \details The `QStringView` is especially useful to append
435 /// text from a QString without allocation.
436 bool appendText_(QStringView txt) noexcept
437 {
438 for (const QChar chr : txt) {
439 if (!appendChar_(static_cast<wchar_t>(chr.unicode())))
440 return false;
441 }
442 return true;
443 }
444
445 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends a bounded character range.
446 bool appendTextRange_(const char* txt, size_t len, size_t maxScan = 4096u) noexcept
447 {
448 if (txt == nullptr) return true;
449 const size_t scanLen = (len < maxScan) ? len : maxScan;
450 for (size_t ii = 0u; ii < scanLen; ++ii) {
451 if (!appendChar_(txt[ii])) return false;
452 }
453 return true;
454 }
455
456 /// \brief Sanitizes and appends a bounded character range.
457 bool appendTextRange_(const wchar_t* txt, size_t len, size_t maxScan = 4096u) noexcept
458 {
459 if (txt == nullptr) return true;
460 const size_t scanLen = (len < maxScan) ? len : maxScan;
461 for (size_t ii = 0u; ii < scanLen; ++ii) {
462 if (!appendChar_(txt[ii])) return false;
463 }
464 return true;
465 }

467 /// \brief Appends a fixed-width unsigned decimal value.
468 /// \note Higher order digits are discarded when the value
469 /// exceeds the requested width.
470 /// \param num The unsigned number to append.
471 /// \param digits The fixed number of digits to append.
472 /// \param pad Pad character on the left if needed.
473 bool appendDigits_(std::uint64_t num, size_t digits, char pad = '0') noexcept
474 {
475 if (digits == 0) return true;
476 if (!canAppend_(digits)) return false;
477 pos_ += digits;
478 bool hasDigit = true;
479 for (size_t ii = 0; ii < digits; ++ii) {
480 const size_t idx = pos_ - 1U - ii;
481 if (hasDigit) {
482 buf_[idx] = static_cast<char>('0' + (num % 10U));
483 num /= 10U;
484 if (num == 0U)
485 hasDigit = false;
486 }
487 else {
488 buf_[idx] = pad;
489 }
490 }
491 return true;
492 }
493
494 /// \brief Appends an unsigned decimal value.
495 bool appendDec_(std::uint32_t num) noexcept
496 {
497 const auto digits = DecDigits_(num);
498 return appendDigits_(num, digits);
499 }
500
501 /// \brief Appends a signed decimal value.
502 bool appendDec_(std::int32_t num) noexcept
503 {
504 const bool neg = (num < 0);
505
506 // Safe absolute value for INT_MIN using unsigned modulo arithmetic.
507 const std::uint32_t uNum = neg
508 ? (std::uint32_t{0} - static_cast<std::uint32_t>(num))
509 : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(num);
510
511 const size_t digits = DecDigits_(uNum);
512 const size_t len = digits + (neg ? 1U : 0U);
513 if (!canAppend_(len)) return false;
514 if (neg) buf_[pos_++] = '-';
515 return appendDigits_(uNum, digits);
516 }
517
518 /// \brief Appends a 32-bit value as fixed-width hexadecimal text.
519 bool appendHex_(std::uint32_t val) noexcept
520 {
521 if (!canAppend_(10u)) return false;
522 buf_[pos_++] = '0';
523 buf_[pos_++] = 'x';
524 for (int ii = 7; ii >= 0; --ii) {
525 const std::uint32_t nib = (val >> (ii * 4)) & 0xFU;
526 buf_[pos_++] = HexDigits_[nib];
527 }
528 return true;
529 }
530
531 /// \brief Terminates the current line and prepares the next fixed-size segment.
532 void finalize_() noexcept
533 {
534 if (end_ <= beg_) return;
535 if (pos_ >= end_) pos_ = end_ - 1u;
536
537 // Remove the trailing spaces
538 while (pos_ > beg_ && buf_[pos_ - 1u] == ' ')
539 --pos_;
540
541 buf_[pos_] = '\0';
542 beg_ = pos_;
543
544 // If the buffer contains less than line size bytes then
545 // assign end as beg so that no new characters could be added.
546 const size_t remaining = Capacity_ - beg_;
547 end_ = remaining >= LineSize_ ? beg_ + LineSize_ : beg_;
548 }
549
550 /// \brief Terminates the current line with CRLF and prepares the next segment.
551 void finalizeAsNewLine_() noexcept
552 {
553 if (end_ <= beg_ || end_ - beg_ < 3u) return;
554 if (pos_ > end_ - 3u) pos_ = end_ - 3u;
555
556 // Remove the trailing spaces
557 while (pos_ > beg_ && buf_[pos_ - 1u] == ' ')
558 --pos_;
559
560 buf_[pos_++] = '\r';
561 buf_[pos_++] = '\n';
562 buf_[pos_] = '\0';
563 beg_ = pos_;
564
565 // If the buffer contains less than line size bytes then
566 // assign end as beg so that no new characters could be added.
567 const size_t remaining = Capacity_ - beg_;
568 end_ = remaining >= LineSize_ ? beg_ + LineSize_ : beg_;
569 }
570
571 private:
572 char buf_[Capacity_]; ///< Fixed-capacity storage for all buffered lines.
573 size_t pos_{0}; ///< Index of the next character to be written.
574 size_t beg_{0}; ///< Starting index of the current line.
575 size_t end_{LineSize};
576 ///< One-past-end index of the current line storage, including space for the terminating '\0'.
577
578 static constexpr char HexDigits_[] = "0123456789ABCDEF"; ///< Lookup table for uppercase hexadecimal digits.
579
580 /// \brief Returns the decimal digit count of a 32-bit unsigned value.
581 static constexpr size_t DecDigits_(std::uint32_t num) noexcept
582 {
583 if (num >= 1000000000U)return 10;
584 if (num >= 100000000U)return 9;
585 if (num >= 10000000U)return 8;
586 if (num >= 1000000U)return 7;
587 if (num >= 100000U)return 6;
588 if (num >= 10000U)return 5;
589 if (num >= 1000U)return 4;
590 if (num >= 100U)return 3;
591 if (num >= 10U)return 2;
592 return 1;
593 }
594 };

596 /**
597 * \brief Caches normalized logging-category text.
598 *
599 * \details
600 * Cache keys are derived from the pointed-to text rather than pointer identity.
601 * Entries are inserted concurrently, published with atomic state transitions,
602 * and stored in a fixed text pool. Slot zero represents an unavailable value.
603 */
604 class CategoryCache final {
605 public:
606 CategoryCache() = default; ///< Default constructor
607 ~CategoryCache() = default; ///< Default destructor
608
609 CategoryCache(const CategoryCache&) = delete; ///< deleted copy constructor
610 CategoryCache& operator=(const CategoryCache&) = delete; ///< deleted copy assignment operator
611
612 CategoryCache(CategoryCache&&) = delete; ///< deleted move constructor
613 CategoryCache& operator=(CategoryCache&&) = delete; ///< deleted move assignment operator
614
615 /// \brief Finds or inserts the normalized category value and returns its slot.
616 /// \return Slot value or null slot (0) if unable to find or insert.
617 std::uint8_t slot_(const QMessageLogContext& ctx) noexcept
618 {
619 const Key key{MakeKey_(ctx.category)};
620 const std::uint32_t start{HashKey_(key) & HashMask_};
621 for (std::uint32_t probe = 0; probe < Capacity_; ++probe) {
622 const std::uint32_t idx{(start + probe) & HashMask_};
623
624 // idx + 1 would be 256, which cannot fit in std::uint8_t.
625 if (idx == UnusableIndex_) continue;
626
627 Entry& entry{entries_[idx]};
628
629 std::uint8_t state{WaitState_(entry)};
630
631 if (state == StateBusy_) {
632 state = WaitState_(entry);
633 if (state == StateBusy_)
634 continue;
635 }
636
637 if (state == StateReady_) {
638 if (KeysEqual_(entry.key_, key))
639 return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(idx + 1u);
640 continue;
641 }
642
643 std::uint8_t expected{StateEmpty_};
644
645 if (!entry.state_.compare_exchange_strong(
646 expected,
647 StateBusy_,
648 std::memory_order_acq_rel,
649 std::memory_order_acquire)) {
650 state = WaitState_(entry);
651 if (state == StateReady_ && KeysEqual_(entry.key_, key))
652 return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(idx + 1u);
653 continue;
654 }
655
656 TextBuffer<TextCap_> buf;
657 Normalize_(buf, ctx.category);
658 const std::size_t textSize{buf.size_()};
659
660 if (textSize == 0u || textSize > std::numeric_limits<std::uint16_t>::max()) {
661 entry.state_.store(StateEmpty_, std::memory_order_release);
662 return NullSlot_;
663 }
664
665 const std::uint16_t length{static_cast<std::uint16_t>(textSize)};
666 const std::uint32_t offset{reservePool_(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(length) + 1u)};
667
668 if (offset == 0u) {
669 entry.state_.store(StateEmpty_, std::memory_order_release);
670 return NullSlot_;
671 }
672
673 std::memcpy(pool_.data() + offset, buf.data_(), length);
674
675 pool_[offset + length] = '\0';
676
677 entry.key_ = key;
678 entry.offset_ = offset;
679 entry.length_ = length;
680 entry.state_.store(StateReady_, std::memory_order_release);
681
682 return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(idx + 1u);
683 }
684 return NullSlot_;
685 }
686
687 /// \brief Returns the immutable text and length associated with a cache slot.
688 /// \return A pair with first value as pointer and second value as length.
689 std::pair<const char*, std::uint16_t> data_(std::uint8_t slot) const noexcept
690 {
691 if (slot == NullSlot_)
692 return {"", 0};
693
694 const std::uint32_t idx{static_cast<std::uint32_t>(slot) - 1u};
695
696 if (idx >= UnusableIndex_)
697 return {"", 0};
698
699 const Entry& entry{entries_[idx]};
700
701 if (entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != StateReady_)
702 return {"", 0};
703
704 if (entry.offset_ == 0u || entry.length_ == 0u)
705 return {"", 0};
706
707 if (entry.offset_ >= PoolSize_)
708 return {"", 0};
709
710 if (entry.length_ >= PoolSize_ - entry.offset_)
711 return {"", 0};
712
713 return {pool_.data() + entry.offset_, entry.length_};
714 }
715
716 private:
717 static constexpr std::uint8_t NullSlot_{0}; ///< First slot is treated as null, returned when no entry exists
718
719 static constexpr std::uint32_t Capacity_{256u}; ///< Total capacity of slots
720 static constexpr std::uint32_t HashMask_{Capacity_ - 1u}; ///< hash mask for creating the key
721
722 /// \brief Since first slot is null, we treat last index as unusable, and all index is stored as index + 1 internally.
723 static constexpr std::uint32_t UnusableIndex_{Capacity_ - 1u};
724
725 static constexpr std::uint32_t PoolSize_{128u * 1024u};
726 ///< Total pool size, the maximum number of bytes this cache can hold
727 static constexpr std::size_t TextCap_{256u}; ///< Maximum number of characters in a single slot
728 static constexpr std::uint32_t ContextScanMax_{2048u}; ///< Maximum number of characters to scan to generate the text
729
730 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateEmpty_{0}; ///< Slot empty state
731 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateBusy_{1}; ///< Slot busy state, when in the middle of being assigned
732 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateReady_{2}; ///< Slot ready state, set to this state after text has been copied to the pool
733
734 static constexpr std::uint32_t BusySpinCount_{256u}; ///< Maximum number of loop iterations to check for a slot being ready after detecting it is busy
735
736 static_assert((Capacity_ & (Capacity_ - 1u)) == 0u);
737 static_assert(Capacity_ == 256u);
738 static_assert(TextCap_ < PoolSize_);
739 static_assert(TextCap_ <= std::numeric_limits<std::uint16_t>::max());
740
741 /// \brief Hash content of text
742 struct TextHash {
743 std::uint64_t hash_{0};
744 std::uint32_t length_{0};
745 };
746
747 /// \brief Single key for a slot
748 struct Key {
749 std::uint64_t hash_{0};
750 std::uint32_t length_{0};
751 };
752
753 /// \brief One entry in the cache
754 struct Entry {
755 Key key_{};
756 std::uint32_t offset_{0};
757 std::uint16_t length_{0};
758 std::atomic<std::uint8_t> state_{StateEmpty_};
759 };
760
761 std::array<Entry, Capacity_> entries_{}; ///< Array of slots entries
762 std::array<char, PoolSize_> pool_{}; ///< Character pool
763 std::atomic<std::uint32_t> poolUsed_{1u}; ///< Index till where the pool has been used, starts at 1 because 0 is null slot
764
765 /// \brief Compares 2 keys for equality.
766 static bool KeysEqual_(const Key& lhs, const Key& rhs) noexcept
767 {
768 return lhs.hash_ == rhs.hash_ && lhs.length_ == rhs.length_;
769 }
770
771 /// \brief Waits briefly for an entry insertion to finish and returns its observed state.
772 static std::uint8_t WaitState_(const Entry& entry) noexcept
773 {
774 std::uint8_t state{entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)};
775 for (std::uint32_t spin = 0; state == StateBusy_ && spin < BusySpinCount_; ++spin) {
776 if ((spin & 15u) == 15u)
777 ::YieldProcessor(); // pause after every 16 failed spins
778 state = entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
779 }
780 return state;
781 }
782
783 /// \brief Hashes bounded null-terminated text and records the scanned length.
784 static TextHash HashText_(const char* text) noexcept
785 {
786 constexpr std::uint64_t OffsetBasis{14695981039346656037ULL};
787 constexpr std::uint64_t Prime{1099511628211ULL};
788
789 TextHash result{
790 .hash_ = OffsetBasis,
791 .length_ = 0
792 };
793
794 if (text == nullptr)
795 return result;
796
797 const auto* current{reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(text)};
798
799 while (*current != '\0' && result.length_ < ContextScanMax_) {
800 result.hash_ ^= static_cast<std::uint64_t>(*current);
801 result.hash_ *= Prime;
802
803 ++current;
804 ++result.length_;
805 }
806
807 return result;
808 }
809
810 /// \brief Builds the cache key from the relevant message-context data.
811 static Key MakeKey_(const char* category) noexcept
812 {
813 const TextHash text{HashText_(category)};
814
815 return {
816 .hash_ = text.hash_,
817 .length_ = text.length_
818 };
819 }
820
821 /// \brief Combines another value into a 64-bit hash state.
822 static void Mix_(std::uint64_t& hash, std::uint64_t value) noexcept
823 {
824 // 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ull is derived from the golden ratio and is commonly
825 // used to spread bits when combining hash values.
826 // (hash << 6u) + (hash >> 2u) makes the new value depend on shifted versions
827 // of the previous hash, so the order of mixed fields matters.
828 hash ^= value + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL + (hash << 6u) + (hash >> 2u);
829 }
830
831 /// \brief Finalizes a cache key into the 32-bit probe hash.
832 static std::uint32_t HashKey_(const Key& key) noexcept
833 {
834 std::uint64_t hash{key.hash_};
835
836 Mix_(hash, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(key.length_));
837
838 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
839 hash *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccdULL;
840 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
841 hash *= 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53ULL;
842 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
843
844 return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(hash ^ (hash >> 32u));
845 }
846
847 /// \brief Atomically reserves a unique contiguous range in the fixed text pool.
848 std::uint32_t reservePool_(std::uint32_t size) noexcept
849 {
850 if (size == 0u || size >= PoolSize_)
851 return 0u;
852
853 // poolUsed_ starts at 1 and position 0 is unused. This is so that
854 // this function can return 0 as invalid/failed marker.
855 std::uint32_t current{poolUsed_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)};
856
857 // Use a compare-exchange loop to reserve a contiguous block of the pool.
858 // The loop retries if another thread reserves space concurrently,
859 // causing the current value to change.
860 // Relaxed ordering is sufficient here because this atomic only reserves
861 // unique pool ranges. Publication happens through entry.state_.
862 while (true) {
863 if (current >= PoolSize_ || size > PoolSize_ - current)
864 return 0u;
865
866 const std::uint32_t next{current + size};
867
868 // Attempt to update poolUsed_ to the new value. If another thread has
869 // modified poolUsed_ since we loaded it, the compare_exchange_weak will
870 // fail, update current with the new value of poolUsed_, and retry the loop.
871 if (poolUsed_.compare_exchange_weak(
872 current,
873 next,
874 std::memory_order_relaxed,
875 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
876 return current;
877 }
878 }
879 }
880
881 /// \brief Normalizes source text into the cache storage format.
882 static void Normalize_(TextBuffer<TextCap_>& buf, const char* category) noexcept
883 {
884 if (category != nullptr && category[0] != '\0')
885 buf.appendText_(category, ContextScanMax_);
886 else
887 buf.appendRawChar_('?');
888 buf.finalize_();
889 }
890 };
891
892 /**
893 * \brief Caches normalized source-file and line-number text.
894 * \details
895 * The cache keeps the last three path components when available, appends the
896 * source line, and stores the result in a fixed pool. Entries are addressed by
897 * compact 16-bit slots carried by `OneLog`.
898 */
899 class FileLineCache final {
900 public:
901 FileLineCache() = default; ///< Default constructor
902 ~FileLineCache() = default; ///< Default destructor
903
904 FileLineCache(const FileLineCache&) = delete; ///< Deleted copy constructor
905 FileLineCache& operator=(const FileLineCache&) = delete; ///< Deleted copy assignment operator
906
907 FileLineCache(FileLineCache&&) = delete; ///< Deleted move constructor
908 FileLineCache& operator=(FileLineCache&&) = delete; ///< Deleted move assignment operator
909
910 /// \brief Finds or inserts the normalized file and line value and returns its slot.
911 /// \return Slot value or null slot (0) if unable to find or insert.
912 std::uint16_t slot_(const QMessageLogContext& ctx) noexcept
913 {
914 const Key key{MakeKey_(ctx)};
915 const std::uint32_t start{HashKey_(key) & HashMask_};
916 for (std::uint32_t probe = 0; probe < Capacity_; ++probe) {
917 const std::uint32_t idx{(start + probe) & HashMask_};
918
919 // idx + 1 would be 65536, which cannot fit in std::uint16_t.
920 if (idx == UnusableIndex_)
921 continue;
922
923 Entry& entry{entries_[idx]};
924
925 std::uint8_t state{WaitState_(entry)};
926
927 if (state == StateBusy_) {
928 state = WaitState_(entry);
929 if (state == StateBusy_)
930 continue;
931 }
932
933 if (state == StateReady_) {
934 if (KeysEqual_(entry.key_, key))
935 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(idx + 1u);
936 continue;
937 }
938
939 std::uint8_t expected{StateEmpty_};
940
941 if (!entry.state_.compare_exchange_strong(
942 expected,
943 StateBusy_,
944 std::memory_order_acq_rel,
945 std::memory_order_acquire)) {
946 state = WaitState_(entry);
947 if (state == StateReady_ && KeysEqual_(entry.key_, key))
948 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(idx + 1u);
949 continue;
950 }
951
952 TextBuffer<TextCap_> buf;
953 Normalize_(buf, ctx);
954 const std::size_t textSize{buf.size_()};
955
956 if (textSize == 0u || textSize > std::numeric_limits<std::uint16_t>::max()) {
957 entry.state_.store(StateEmpty_, std::memory_order_release);
958 return NullSlot_;
959 }
960
961 const std::uint16_t length{static_cast<std::uint16_t>(textSize)};
962
963 const std::uint32_t offset{reservePool_(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(length) + 1u)};
964
965 if (offset == 0u) {
966 entry.state_.store(StateEmpty_, std::memory_order_release);
967 return NullSlot_;
968 }
969
970 std::memcpy(pool_.data() + offset, buf.data_(), length);
971
972 pool_[offset + length] = '\0';
973
974 entry.key_ = key;
975 entry.offset_ = offset;
976 entry.length_ = length;
977 entry.state_.store(StateReady_, std::memory_order_release);
978
979 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(idx + 1u);
980 }
981 return NullSlot_;
982 }
983
984 /// \brief Returns the immutable text and length associated with a cache slot.
985 /// \return A pair with first value as pointer and second value as length.
986 std::pair<const char*, std::uint16_t> data_(std::uint16_t slot) const noexcept
987 {
988 if (slot == NullSlot_)
989 return {"", 0};
990
991 const std::uint32_t idx{static_cast<std::uint32_t>(slot) - 1u};
992
993 if (idx >= UnusableIndex_)
994 return {"", 0};
995
996 const Entry& entry{entries_[idx]};
997
998 if (entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != StateReady_)
999 return {"", 0};
1000
1001 if (entry.offset_ == 0u || entry.length_ == 0u)
1002 return {"", 0};
1003
1004 if (entry.offset_ >= PoolSize_)
1005 return {"", 0};
1006
1007 if (entry.length_ >= PoolSize_ - entry.offset_)
1008 return {"", 0};
1009
1010 return {pool_.data() + entry.offset_, entry.length_};
1011 }
1012
1013 private:
1014 static constexpr std::uint16_t NullSlot_{0}; ///< First slot is treated as null, returned when no entry exists
1015
1016 static constexpr std::uint32_t Capacity_{65536u}; ///< Total number of slots
1017 static constexpr std::uint32_t HashMask_{Capacity_ - 1u}; ///< Hash mask for creating the key
1018 static constexpr std::uint32_t UnusableIndex_{Capacity_ - 1u}; ///< Since first slot is null, we treat last index as unusable, and all index is stored as index + 1 internally
1019
1020 static constexpr std::uint32_t PoolSize_{8u * 1024u * 1024u}; ///< Total pool size, the maximum number of bytes this cache can hold
1021 static constexpr std::size_t TextCap_{256u}; ///< Maximum number of characters in a single slot
1022 static constexpr std::uint32_t ContextScanMax_{2048u}; ///< Maximum number of characters to scan to generate the text
1023
1024 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateEmpty_{0}; ///< Slot empty state
1025 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateBusy_{1}; ///< Slot busy state, when in the middle of being assigned
1026 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateReady_{2}; ///< Slot ready state, set to this state after text has been copied to the pool
1027
1028 static constexpr std::uint32_t BusySpinCount_{256u}; ///< Maximum number of loop iterations to check for a slot being ready after detecting it is busy
1029
1030 static_assert((Capacity_ & (Capacity_ - 1u)) == 0u);
1031 static_assert(Capacity_ == 65536u);
1032 static_assert(TextCap_ < PoolSize_);
1033 static_assert(TextCap_ <= std::numeric_limits<std::uint16_t>::max());
1034
1035 /// \brief Hash content of text
1036 struct TextHash {
1037 std::uint64_t hash_{0};
1038 std::uint32_t length_{0};
1039 };
1040
1041 /// \brief Single key for a slot
1042 struct Key {
1043 std::uint64_t fileHash_{0};
1044 std::uint32_t fileLength_{0};
1045 std::int32_t line_{0};
1046 };
1047
1048 /// \brief One entry in the cache
1049 struct Entry {
1050 Key key_{};
1051 std::uint32_t offset_{0};
1052 std::uint16_t length_{0};
1053 std::atomic<std::uint8_t> state_{StateEmpty_};
1054 };
1055
1056 std::array<Entry, Capacity_> entries_{}; ///< Array of slots entries
1057 std::array<char, PoolSize_> pool_{}; ///< Character pool
1058 std::atomic<std::uint32_t> poolUsed_{1u}; ///< Index till where the pool has been used, starts at 1 because 0 is null slot
1059
1060 /// \brief Compares 2 keys for equality.
1061 static bool KeysEqual_(const Key& lhs, const Key& rhs) noexcept
1062 {
1063 return lhs.fileHash_ == rhs.fileHash_ &&
1064 lhs.fileLength_ == rhs.fileLength_ &&
1065 lhs.line_ == rhs.line_;
1066 }
1067
1068 /// \brief Waits briefly for an entry insertion to finish and returns its observed state.
1069 static std::uint8_t WaitState_(const Entry& entry) noexcept
1070 {
1071 std::uint8_t state{entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)};
1072 for (std::uint32_t spin = 0; state == StateBusy_ && spin < BusySpinCount_; ++spin) {
1073 if ((spin & 15u) == 15u)
1074 ::YieldProcessor(); // pause after every 16 failed spins
1075 state = entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
1076 }
1077 return state;
1078 }
1079
1080 /// \brief Hashes bounded null-terminated text and records the scanned length.
1081 static TextHash HashText_(const char* text) noexcept
1082 {
1083 constexpr std::uint64_t OffsetBasis{14695981039346656037ULL};
1084
1085 constexpr std::uint64_t Prime{1099511628211ULL};
1086
1087 TextHash result{
1088 .hash_ = OffsetBasis,
1089 .length_ = 0
1090 };
1091
1092 if (text == nullptr)
1093 return result;
1094
1095 const auto* current{reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(text)};
1096
1097 while (*current != '\0' && result.length_ < ContextScanMax_) {
1098 result.hash_ ^= static_cast<std::uint64_t>(*current);
1099 result.hash_ *= Prime;
1100
1101 ++current;
1102 ++result.length_;
1103 }
1104
1105 return result;
1106 }
1107
1108 /// \brief Builds the cache key from the relevant message-context data.
1109 static Key MakeKey_(const QMessageLogContext& ctx) noexcept
1110 {
1111 const TextHash file{HashText_(ctx.file)};
1112
1113 return {
1114 .fileHash_ = file.hash_,
1115 .fileLength_ = file.length_,
1116 .line_ = ctx.line
1117 };
1118 }
1119
1120 /// \brief Combines another value into a 64-bit hash state.
1121 static void Mix_(std::uint64_t& hash, std::uint64_t value) noexcept
1122 {
1123 // 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ull is derived from the golden ratio and is commonly
1124 // used to spread bits when combining hash values.
1125 // (hash << 6u) + (hash >> 2u) makes the new value depend on shifted versions
1126 // of the previous hash, so the order of mixed fields matters.
1127 hash ^= value + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL + (hash << 6u) + (hash >> 2u);
1128 }
1129
1130 /// \brief Finalizes a cache key into the 32-bit probe hash.
1131 static std::uint32_t HashKey_(const Key& key) noexcept
1132 {
1133 std::uint64_t hash{key.fileHash_};
1134
1135 const std::uint64_t lengthAndLine{
1136 (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(key.fileLength_) << 32u) |
1137 static_cast<std::uint64_t>(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(key.line_))
1138 };
1139
1140 Mix_(hash, lengthAndLine);
1141
1142 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
1143 hash *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccdULL;
1144 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
1145 hash *= 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53ULL;
1146 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
1147
1148 return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(hash ^ (hash >> 32u));
1149 }
1150
1151 /// \brief Atomically reserves a unique contiguous range in the fixed text pool.
1152 std::uint32_t reservePool_(std::uint32_t size) noexcept
1153 {
1154 if (size == 0u || size >= PoolSize_)
1155 return 0u;
1156
1157 std::uint32_t current{poolUsed_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)};
1158
1159 while (true) {
1160 if (current >= PoolSize_ || size > PoolSize_ - current)
1161 return 0u;
1162
1163 const std::uint32_t next{current + size};
1164
1165 if (poolUsed_.compare_exchange_weak(
1166 current,
1167 next,
1168 std::memory_order_relaxed,
1169 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
1170 return current;
1171 }
1172 }
1173 }
1174
1175 /// \brief Appends the retained source-path components used by the file-line field.
1176 static bool AppendFileName_(TextBuffer<TextCap_>& buf, const char* file) noexcept
1177 {
1178 if (file == nullptr || file[0] == '\0')
1179 return buf.appendRawChar_('?');
1180
1181 std::size_t sep1{0};
1182 std::size_t sep2{0};
1183 std::size_t sep3{0};
1184 std::size_t last{0};
1185
1186 while (last < ContextScanMax_ && file[last] != '\0') {
1187 if (file[last] == '\\' || file[last] == '/') {
1188 sep1 = sep2;
1189 sep2 = sep3;
1190 sep3 = last + 1u;
1191 }
1192 ++last;
1193 }
1194
1195 if (last == 0u || sep3 == last)
1196 return buf.appendRawChar_('?');
1197
1198 return buf.appendTextRange_(file + sep1, last - sep1);
1199 }
1200
1201 /// \brief Normalizes source text into the cache storage format.
1202 static void Normalize_(TextBuffer<TextCap_>& buf, const QMessageLogContext& ctx) noexcept
1203 {
1204 bool ok{AppendFileName_(buf, ctx.file)};
1205 if (ok) ok = buf.appendRawChar_(':');
1206 if (ok) buf.appendDec_(ctx.line);
1207 buf.finalize_();
1208 }
1209 };

1211 /**
1212 * \brief Caches normalized function names from Qt message contexts.
1213 * \details
1214 * Return types and parameter lists are removed while operator names, qualifiers,
1215 * scopes, and template arguments are retained on a best-effort basis. Entries are
1216 * stored in a fixed pool and referenced by compact 16-bit slots.
1217 */
1218 class FunctionCache final {
1219 public:
1220 FunctionCache() = default; ///< Default constructor
1221 ~FunctionCache() = default; ///< Default destructor
1222
1223 FunctionCache(const FunctionCache&) = delete; ///< Deleted copy constructor
1224 FunctionCache& operator=(const FunctionCache&) = delete; ///< Deleted copy assignment operator
1225
1226 FunctionCache(FunctionCache&&) = delete; ///< Deleted move constructor
1227 FunctionCache& operator=(FunctionCache&&) = delete; ///< Deleted move assignment operator
1228
1229 /// \brief Finds or inserts the normalized function value and returns its slot.
1230 /// \return Slot value or null slot (0) if unable to find or insert.
1231 std::uint16_t slot_(const QMessageLogContext& ctx) noexcept
1232 {
1233 const Key key{MakeKey_(ctx.function)};
1234 const std::uint32_t start{HashKey_(key) & HashMask_};
1235 for (std::uint32_t probe = 0; probe < Capacity_; ++probe) {
1236 const std::uint32_t idx{(start + probe) & HashMask_};
1237
1238 // idx + 1 would be 65536, which cannot fit in std::uint16_t.
1239 if (idx == UnusableIndex_)
1240 continue;
1241
1242 Entry& entry{entries_[idx]};
1243
1244 std::uint8_t state{WaitState_(entry)};
1245 if (state == StateBusy_) {
1246 state = WaitState_(entry);
1247 if (state == StateBusy_)
1248 continue;
1249 }
1250
1251 if (state == StateReady_) {
1252 if (KeysEqual_(entry.key_, key))
1253 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(idx + 1u);
1254 continue;
1255 }
1256
1257 std::uint8_t expected{StateEmpty_};
1258
1259 if (!entry.state_.compare_exchange_strong(
1260 expected,
1261 StateBusy_,
1262 std::memory_order_acq_rel,
1263 std::memory_order_acquire)) {
1264 state = WaitState_(entry);
1265 if (state == StateReady_ && KeysEqual_(entry.key_, key))
1266 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(idx + 1u);
1267 continue;
1268 }
1269
1270 TextBuffer<TextCap_> buf;
1271 Normalize_(buf, ctx.function);
1272 const std::size_t textSize{buf.size_()};
1273
1274 if (textSize == 0u || textSize > std::numeric_limits<std::uint16_t>::max()) {
1275 entry.state_.store(StateEmpty_, std::memory_order_release);
1276 return NullSlot_;
1277 }
1278
1279 const std::uint16_t length{static_cast<std::uint16_t>(textSize)};
1280
1281 const std::uint32_t offset{reservePool_(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(length) + 1u)};
1282
1283 if (offset == 0u) {
1284 entry.state_.store(StateEmpty_, std::memory_order_release);
1285 return NullSlot_;
1286 }
1287
1288 std::memcpy(pool_.data() + offset, buf.data_(), length);
1289
1290 pool_[offset + length] = '\0';
1291
1292 entry.key_ = key;
1293 entry.offset_ = offset;
1294 entry.length_ = length;
1295 entry.state_.store(StateReady_, std::memory_order_release);
1296
1297 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(idx + 1u);
1298 }
1299
1300 return NullSlot_;
1301 }
1302
1303 /// \brief Returns the immutable text and length associated with a cache slot.
1304 /// \return A pair with first value as pointer and second value as length.
1305 std::pair<const char*, std::uint16_t> data_(std::uint16_t slot) const noexcept
1306 {
1307 if (slot == NullSlot_)
1308 return {"", 0};
1309
1310 const std::uint32_t idx{static_cast<std::uint32_t>(slot) - 1u};
1311
1312 if (idx >= UnusableIndex_)
1313 return {"", 0};
1314
1315 const Entry& entry{entries_[idx]};
1316
1317 if (entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != StateReady_)
1318 return {"", 0};
1319
1320 if (entry.offset_ == 0u || entry.length_ == 0u)
1321 return {"", 0};
1322
1323 if (entry.offset_ >= PoolSize_)
1324 return {"", 0};
1325
1326 if (entry.length_ >= PoolSize_ - entry.offset_)
1327 return {"", 0};
1328
1329 return {
1330 pool_.data() + entry.offset_,
1331 entry.length_
1332 };
1333 }
1334
1335 private:
1336 static constexpr std::uint16_t NullSlot_{0}; ///< First slot is treated as null, returned when no entry exists
1337
1338 static constexpr std::uint32_t Capacity_{65536u}; ///< Total capacity of slots
1339 static constexpr std::uint32_t HashMask_{Capacity_ - 1u}; ///< Hash mask for creating the key
1340 static constexpr std::uint32_t UnusableIndex_{Capacity_ - 1u}; ///< Since first slot is null, we treat last index as unusable, and all index is stored as index + 1 internally
1341
1342 static constexpr std::uint32_t PoolSize_{16u * 1024u * 1024u}; ///< Total pool size, the maximum number of bytes this cache can hold
1343 static constexpr std::size_t TextCap_{256u}; ///< Maximum number of characters in a single slot
1344 static constexpr std::uint32_t ContextScanMax_{2048u}; ///< Maximum number of characters to scan to generate the text
1345
1346 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateEmpty_{0}; ///< Slot empty state
1347 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateBusy_{1}; ///< Slot busy state, when in the middle of being assigned
1348 static constexpr std::uint8_t StateReady_{2}; ///< Slot ready state, set to this state after text has been copied to the pool
1349
1350 static constexpr std::uint32_t BusySpinCount_{256u}; ///< Maximum number of loop iterations to check for a slot being ready after detecting it is busy
1351
1352 static_assert((Capacity_ & (Capacity_ - 1u)) == 0u);
1353 static_assert(Capacity_ == 65536u);
1354 static_assert(TextCap_ < PoolSize_);
1355 static_assert(TextCap_ <= std::numeric_limits<std::uint16_t>::max());
1356
1357 /// \brief Hash content of text
1358 struct TextHash {
1359 std::uint64_t hash_{0};
1360 std::uint32_t length_{0};
1361 };
1362
1363 /// \brief Single key for a slot
1364 struct Key {
1365 std::uint64_t hash_{0};
1366 std::uint32_t length_{0};
1367 };
1368
1369 /// \brief One entry in the cache
1370 struct Entry {
1371 Key key_{};
1372 std::uint32_t offset_{0};
1373 std::uint16_t length_{0};
1374 std::atomic<std::uint8_t> state_{StateEmpty_};
1375 };
1376
1377 std::array<Entry, Capacity_> entries_{}; ///< Array of slots entries
1378 std::array<char, PoolSize_> pool_{}; ///< Character pool
1379 std::atomic<std::uint32_t> poolUsed_{1u}; ///< Index till where the pool has been used, starts at 1 because 0 is null slot
1380
1381 /// \brief Compares 2 keys for equality.
1382 static bool KeysEqual_(const Key& lhs, const Key& rhs) noexcept
1383 {
1384 return lhs.hash_ == rhs.hash_ && lhs.length_ == rhs.length_;
1385 }
1386
1387 /// \brief Waits briefly for an entry insertion to finish and returns its observed state.
1388 static std::uint8_t WaitState_(const Entry& entry) noexcept
1389 {
1390 std::uint8_t state{entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)};
1391 for (std::uint32_t spin = 0; state == StateBusy_ && spin < BusySpinCount_; ++spin) {
1392 if ((spin & 15u) == 15u)
1393 ::YieldProcessor();
1394 state = entry.state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
1395 }
1396 return state;
1397 }
1398
1399 /// \brief Hashes bounded null-terminated text and records the scanned length.
1400 static TextHash HashText_(const char* text) noexcept
1401 {
1402 constexpr std::uint64_t OffsetBasis{14695981039346656037ULL};
1403 constexpr std::uint64_t Prime{1099511628211ULL};
1404
1405 TextHash result{
1406 .hash_ = OffsetBasis,
1407 .length_ = 0
1408 };
1409
1410 if (text == nullptr)
1411 return result;
1412
1413 const auto* current{reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(text)};
1414
1415 while (*current != '\0' && result.length_ < ContextScanMax_) {
1416 result.hash_ ^= static_cast<std::uint64_t>(*current);
1417 result.hash_ *= Prime;
1418
1419 ++current;
1420 ++result.length_;
1421 }
1422
1423 return result;
1424 }
1425
1426 /// \brief Builds the cache key from the relevant message-context data.
1427 static Key MakeKey_(const char* function) noexcept
1428 {
1429 const TextHash text{HashText_(function)};
1430
1431 return {
1432 .hash_ = text.hash_,
1433 .length_ = text.length_
1434 };
1435 }
1436
1437 /// \brief Combines another value into a 64-bit hash state.
1438 static void Mix_(std::uint64_t& hash, std::uint64_t value) noexcept
1439 {
1440 hash ^= value + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL + (hash << 6u) + (hash >> 2u);
1441 }
1442
1443 /// \brief Finalizes a cache key into the 32-bit probe hash.
1444 static std::uint32_t HashKey_(const Key& key) noexcept
1445 {
1446 std::uint64_t hash{key.hash_};
1447
1448 Mix_(hash, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(key.length_));
1449
1450 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
1451 hash *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccdULL;
1452 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
1453 hash *= 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53ULL;
1454 hash ^= hash >> 33u;
1455
1456 return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(hash ^ (hash >> 32u));
1457 }
1458
1459 /// \brief Atomically reserves a unique contiguous range in the fixed text pool.
1460 std::uint32_t reservePool_(std::uint32_t size) noexcept
1461 {
1462 if (size == 0u || size >= PoolSize_)
1463 return 0u;
1464
1465 std::uint32_t current{poolUsed_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)};
1466
1467 while (true) {
1468 if (current >= PoolSize_ || size > PoolSize_ - current)
1469 return 0u;
1470
1471 const std::uint32_t next{current + size};
1472
1473 if (poolUsed_.compare_exchange_weak(
1474 current,
1475 next,
1476 std::memory_order_relaxed,
1477 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
1478 return current;
1479 }
1480 }
1481 }
1482
1483 /// \brief Checks whether a byte is recognized as whitespace.
1484 static constexpr bool IsSpaceChar_(char chr) noexcept
1485 {
1486 return chr == ' ' || chr == '\t' || chr == '\r' ||
1487 chr == '\n' || chr == '\v' || chr == '\f';
1488 }
1489
1490 /// \brief Checks whether a byte can occur in a C++ identifier.
1491 static constexpr bool IsIdentifierChar_(char chr) noexcept
1492 {
1493 return
1494 (chr >= 'a' && chr <= 'z') ||
1495 (chr >= 'A' && chr <= 'Z') ||
1496 (chr >= '0' && chr <= '9') ||
1497 chr == '_';
1498 }
1499
1500 /// \brief Extracts and appends the display form of a C++ function name.
1501 static bool AppendFunction_(TextBuffer<TextCap_>& buf, const char* function) noexcept
1502 {
1503 if (function == nullptr || function[0] == '\0')
1504 return buf.appendRawChar_('?');
1505
1506 const char* end = function;
1507 for (size_t n = 0; n < ContextScanMax_ && *end != '\0' && *end != '('; ++n)
1508 ++end;
1509
1510 if (end == function)
1511 return buf.appendRawChar_('?');
1512
1513 const char* ope = nullptr;
1514 for (const char* it = function; it < end; ++it) {
1515 if ((end - it) < 8) break;
1516 if (it[0] == 'o' && it[1] == 'p' && it[2] == 'e' && it[3] == 'r' &&
1517 it[4] == 'a' && it[5] == 't' && it[6] == 'o' && it[7] == 'r') {
1518 const bool lftOk = (it == function) || IsSpaceChar_(it[-1]) || it[-1] == ':';
1519 const bool ritOk = ((it + 8) == end) || !IsIdentifierChar_(it[8]);
1520 if (lftOk && ritOk) ope = it;
1521 }
1522 }
1523
1524 const char* space = nullptr;
1525 size_t templateDepth = 0;
1526
1527 const char* it = (ope != nullptr) ? ope : end;
1528
1529 while (it > function) {
1530 --it;
1531
1532 if (*it == '>') {
1533 ++templateDepth;
1534 }
1535 else if (*it == '<') {
1536 if (templateDepth > 0u) {
1537 --templateDepth;
1538 }
1539 }
1540 else if (templateDepth == 0u && IsSpaceChar_(*it)) {
1541 space = it;
1542 break;
1543 }
1544 }
1545
1546 const char* beg = (space != nullptr) ? (space + 1) : function;
1547
1548 while (beg < end && IsSpaceChar_(*beg))
1549 ++beg;
1550
1551 if (beg >= end) return buf.appendRawChar_('?');
1552 const size_t available = static_cast<size_t>(end - beg);
1553 return buf.appendTextRange_(beg, available);
1554 }
1555
1556 /// \brief Normalizes source text into the cache storage format.
1557 static void Normalize_(TextBuffer<TextCap_>& buf, const char* function) noexcept
1558 {
1559 AppendFunction_(buf, function);
1560 buf.finalize_();
1561 }
1562 };
1563

1725 LeakedState(const LeakedState&) = delete; ///< Deleted copy constructor

1727 LeakedState(LeakedState&&) = delete; ///< Deleted move constructor

1731 /// \brief Returns the intentionally leaked process-wide logging state.
1732 static LeakedState& Inst_() noexcept
1733 {
1734 static auto* inst = new LeakedState;
1735 return *inst;
1736 }
1737
1738 private:
1739 /// \brief Private constructor so that only one instance of this class can be created using the static `Inst_()` function
1740 LeakedState() : allFields_{GenAllFieldsText_()},
1741 defFileFieldsText_{GenTextFromFieldsList_(defFileFields_)},
1742 defDispFieldsText_{GenTextFromFieldsList_(defDispFields_)},
1743 permConsole_{PermConsoleHandle_()} {}

1745 /// \brief Generates the space-separated list of every supported output field.
1746 static QString GenAllFieldsText_()
1747 {
1748 constexpr auto allNames = magic_enum::enum_names<Field>();
1749 QString str;
1750 for (auto name : allNames) {
1751 if (!str.isEmpty()) str.append(' ');
1752 str.append(QLatin1StringView{
1753 name.data(),
1754 static_cast<qsizetype>(name.size())
1755 });
1756 }
1757 return str;
1758 }
1759
1760 /// \brief Converts an ordered field list to normalized field text.
1761 static QString GenTextFromFieldsList_(const QList<Field>& fields)
1762 {
1763 QString str;
1764 for (const Field field : fields) {
1765 const auto name = magic_enum::enum_name(field);
1766 if (name.empty()) continue;
1767 if (!str.isEmpty()) str.append(' ');
1768 str.append(QLatin1StringView{
1769 name.data(),
1770 static_cast<qsizetype>(name.size())
1771 });
1772 }
1773 return str;
1774 }
1775
1776 /// \brief Detects and configures the console attached during initialization.
1777 static HANDLE PermConsoleHandle_()
1778 {
1779 // No console was attached when LeakedState was created.
1780 if (::GetConsoleWindow() == nullptr)
1781 return INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
1782
1783 // Open the attached console directly, independently of redirected
1784 // STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE or STD_ERROR_HANDLE.
1785 const HANDLE consoleHandle = ::CreateFileW(
1786 L"CONOUT$",
1787 GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE,
1788 FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE,
1789 nullptr,
1790 OPEN_EXISTING,
1791 0,
1792 nullptr);
1793
1794 if (consoleHandle == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
1795 const DWORD error = ::GetLastError();
1796
1797 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1798 QStringLiteral(
1799 "Fatal Error:\n"
1800 "Permanent Console Initialization Failed.\n\n"
1801 "'CreateFileW(CONOUT$)' failed.\n\n"
1802 "Error: %1\n\n"
1803 "The application cannot continue safely and will now exit.")
1804 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(error))));
1805 }
1806
1807 // Configure console output.
1808 DWORD outMode = 0;
1809 if (::GetConsoleMode(consoleHandle, &outMode) == 0) {
1810 const DWORD error = ::GetLastError();
1811 ::CloseHandle(consoleHandle);
1812
1813 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1814 QStringLiteral(
1815 "Fatal Error:\n"
1816 "Permanent Console Initialization Failed.\n\n"
1817 "'GetConsoleMode' failed for the CONOUT$ handle.\n\n"
1818 "Error: %1\n\n"
1819 "The application cannot continue safely and will now exit.")
1820 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(error))));
1821 }
1822
1823 const DWORD desiredOutMode =
1824 outMode | ENABLE_PROCESSED_OUTPUT | ENABLE_WRAP_AT_EOL_OUTPUT;
1825
1826 if (outMode != desiredOutMode)
1827 (void)::SetConsoleMode(consoleHandle, desiredOutMode);
1828
1829 // Configure console input when STD_INPUT_HANDLE still refers to
1830 // the console rather than a redirected file or pipe.
1831 const HANDLE input = ::GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE);
1832 if (input != nullptr && input != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
1833 DWORD inMode = 0;
1834
1835 if (::GetConsoleMode(input, &inMode)) {
1836 DWORD desiredInMode = inMode | ENABLE_EXTENDED_FLAGS;
1837 desiredInMode &= ~ENABLE_QUICK_EDIT_MODE;
1838 desiredInMode &= ~ENABLE_INSERT_MODE;
1839 desiredInMode &= ~ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT;
1840
1841 if (inMode != desiredInMode)
1842 (void)::SetConsoleMode(input, desiredInMode);
1843 }
1844 }
1845
1846 QString title{QString(npi::app::name).append(" Console")};
1847 (void)::SetConsoleTitleW(
1848 reinterpret_cast<LPCWSTR>(title.utf16()));
1849
1850 return consoleHandle;
1851 }
1852 };
1853
1854 /**
1855 * \brief Manages the external helper process used for important logs.
1856 * \details
1857 * The helper receives formatted records through an anonymous pipe and writes them
1858 * to the primary or backup important-log file. Normal writes are serialized while
1859 * fatal and crash paths use bounded best-effort coordination.
1860 */
1861 namespace bridge
1862 {
1863 constexpr size_t filePathMaxLen = 4096u; ///< Max length for file path, 4096 is generous but safe.
1864
1865 /// \brief Converts an important-log helper exit code to explanatory text.
1866 QString processExitText(DWORD code)
1867 {
1868 switch (code) {
1869 case 0:
1870 return QStringLiteral("Normal shutdown.");
1871 case 1:
1872 return QStringLiteral("Missing/invalid primary log file path argument.");
1873 case 2:
1874 return QStringLiteral("Primary log path ends with a slash.");
1875 case 3:
1876 return QStringLiteral("Backup log path ends with a slash.");
1877 case 4:
1878 return QStringLiteral("Missing/invalid STDIN handle.");
1879 case 5:
1880 return QStringLiteral("STDIN read failed.");
1881 case 6:
1882 return QStringLiteral("Failed to open/create both primary and backup log files.");
1883 case 7:
1884 return QStringLiteral("Failed to open/create primary log file, and no backup was provided.");
1885 case 8:
1886 return QStringLiteral("Log file write failed.");
1887 case 9:
1888 return QStringLiteral("Log file write made no progress after repeated attempts.");
1889 default:
1890 return QStringLiteral("Unknown error.");
1891 }
1892 }
1893
1894 /// \brief Starts a new `npiImpLog.exe` helper for the supplied directory and file base name.
1895 /// \details
1896 /// The new process and pipe handles replace the previous pair only after startup succeeds and no crash or
1897 /// fatal owner has taken control.
1898 /// \param directory Current directory
1899 /// \param fileBaseName current file base name without `.log` or `.imp.log`.
1900 void startProcess(const QString& directory, const QString& fileBaseName)
1901 {
1902 // Construct the primary and backup file full paths for the important log process.
1903 const QString fileName = fileBaseName + QStringLiteral(".imp.log");
1904 const QString pFileStr = QDir(directory).filePath(fileName);
1905 const QString bFileStr = QDir(npi::app::appProgramDataDir()).filePath(QStringLiteral("ImpLogs/%1").arg(fileName));
1906 const std::wstring primaryFullPath = QDir::toNativeSeparators(pFileStr).toStdWString();
1907 const std::wstring backupFullPath = QDir::toNativeSeparators(bFileStr).toStdWString();
1908
1909 LeakedState& leaked = LeakedState::Inst_();
1910
1911 // Path texts checks.
1912
1913 if (primaryFullPath.empty())
1914 npi::app::winStopMsgExe("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\nPrimary log path is empty.");
1915
1916 if (primaryFullPath.back() == L'\\' || primaryFullPath.back() == L'/')
1917 npi::app::winStopMsgExe("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\nPrimary log path ends with a slash.");
1918
1919 if (!backupFullPath.empty() && (backupFullPath.back() == L'\\' || backupFullPath.back() == L'/'))
1920 npi::app::winStopMsgExe("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\nBackup log path ends with a slash.");
1921
1922 // GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, ...) gets the full path of the currently running
1923 // main executable, for example C:\MyApp\bin\MyApp.exe
1924 wchar_t impLogExePathBuf[filePathMaxLen]{};
1925 const DWORD n = ::GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, impLogExePathBuf, filePathMaxLen);
1926 if (n == 0 || n >= filePathMaxLen) {
1927 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
1928 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1929 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'GetModuleFileNameW' Error:\n%1")
1930 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
1931 }
1932
1933 // Construct the helper executable path by replacing the main executable name with npiImpLog.exe.
1934 std::wstring impLogExePath(impLogExePathBuf, impLogExePathBuf + n);
1935 const size_t slash = impLogExePath.find_last_of(L"\\/");
1936 if (slash == std::wstring::npos)
1937 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1938 "Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\nnpiImpLog.exe path could not be determined");
1939 impLogExePath.resize(slash + 1);
1940 impLogExePath += L"npiImpLog.exe";
1941
1942 // Create an inheritable anonymous pipe.
1943 // Child (npiImpLog.exe) gets the read end as stdin.
1944 // Parent (this process) keeps the write end for sending log data.
1945 SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES sa{};
1946 sa.nLength = sizeof(sa);
1947 sa.bInheritHandle = TRUE;
1948
1949 HANDLE hRead = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE; // read handle
1950 HANDLE hWrite = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE; // write handle
1951
1952 // Create the anonymous pipe with a reasonably large buffer to reduce the chance of blocking on writes.
1953 constexpr DWORD pipeBufBytes = 256u * 1024u; // buffer 256 KiB
1954 if (!::CreatePipe(&hRead, &hWrite, &sa, pipeBufBytes)) {
1955 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
1956 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1957 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'CreatePipe' Error:\n%1")
1958 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
1959 }
1960
1961 // Remove inheritance from the write handle. The child must inherit only
1962 // the read end. If it inherits the write end too, EOF detection can
1963 // break because the pipe would still have a writer open.
1964 if (!::SetHandleInformation(hWrite, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, 0)) {
1965 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
1966 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
1967 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
1968 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1969 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'SetHandleInformation' Error:\n%1")
1970 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
1971 }
1972
1973 // The anonymous pipe is used only for the child process's standard input. The
1974 // npiImpLog.exe does not use STDOUT or STDERR. Redirect both streams to NUL
1975 // so the helper does not depend on the parent process having valid console handles,
1976 // which is especially important for GUI applications.
1977 // hNull is created as inheritable because it is explicitly passed to the child
1978 // as STDOUT and STDERR. Unrelated inheritable handles are blocked later by the
1979 // PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST setup.
1980 HANDLE hNull = ::CreateFileW(
1981 L"NUL",
1982 GENERIC_WRITE,
1983 FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE,
1984 &sa,
1985 OPEN_EXISTING,
1986 FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL,
1987 nullptr);
1988
1989 // Check the NUL handle before starting the process.
1990 if (hNull == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE || hNull == nullptr) {
1991 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
1992 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
1993 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
1994 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
1995 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'CreateFileW(NUL)' Error:\n%1")
1996 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
1997 }
1998
1999 // Build command line in format: "npiImpLog.exe" "primary" "backup"
2000 // Paths are quoted because both executable and log paths may contain spaces.
2001 std::wstring cmdLine;
2002 cmdLine.reserve(impLogExePath.size() + primaryFullPath.size() + backupFullPath.size() + 16);
2003 cmdLine += L"\"";
2004 cmdLine += impLogExePath;
2005 cmdLine += L"\" \"";
2006 cmdLine += primaryFullPath;
2007 cmdLine += L"\"";
2008 if (!backupFullPath.empty()) {
2009 cmdLine += L" \"";
2010 cmdLine += backupFullPath;
2011 cmdLine += L"\"";
2012 }
2013
2014 // Restrict inheritance to the exact handles needed by the child process.
2015 HANDLE inheritList[2]{hRead, hNull};
2016
2017 // Ask Windows for the required memory size for one process/thread attribute.
2018 // This first sizing call is expected to fail with ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER
2019 // and return the required byte count in attrListBytes.
2020 SIZE_T attrListBytes = 0;
2021 const BOOL attrSizeOk = ::InitializeProcThreadAttributeList(nullptr, 1, 0, &attrListBytes);
2022 const DWORD attrSizeErr = ::GetLastError();
2023
2024 // For the sizing call, success is unexpected. The valid result is failure with
2025 // ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER and a non-zero attrListBytes value. Anything else
2026 // means Windows did not provide a usable attribute-list size.
2027 if (attrSizeOk || attrListBytes == 0 || attrSizeErr != ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER) {
2028 ::CloseHandle(hNull);
2029 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
2030 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
2031 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2032 QStringLiteral(
2033 "Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'InitializeProcThreadAttributeList' (get size) Error:\n%1")
2034 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(attrSizeErr))));
2035 }
2036
2037 // Allocate the attribute-list buffer using the process heap because Windows
2038 // owns the internal layout of this structure. It is later released with
2039 // HeapFree().
2040 auto* attrList = static_cast<LPPROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_LIST>(
2041 ::HeapAlloc(::GetProcessHeap(), 0, attrListBytes));
2042
2043 if (!attrList) {
2044 ::CloseHandle(hNull);
2045 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
2046 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
2047 npi::app::winStopMsgExe("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'HeapAlloc' failed for attribute list");
2048 }
2049
2050 // Initialize the allocated attribute list. This prepares the buffer so it can
2051 // receive attributes such as the explicit handle inheritance list.
2052 if (!::InitializeProcThreadAttributeList(attrList, 1, 0, &attrListBytes)) {
2053 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
2054 ::HeapFree(::GetProcessHeap(), 0, attrList);
2055 ::CloseHandle(hNull);
2056 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
2057 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
2058 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2059 QStringLiteral(
2060 "Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'InitializeProcThreadAttributeList' Error:\n%1")
2061 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
2062 }
2063
2064 // Restrict child handle inheritance to hRead and hNull only. This prevents the
2065 // child from inheriting unrelated handles, especially the pipe write handle.
2066 if (!::UpdateProcThreadAttribute(
2067 attrList,
2068 0,
2069 PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST,
2070 reinterpret_cast<void*>(inheritList),
2071 sizeof(inheritList),
2072 nullptr,
2073 nullptr)) {
2074 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
2075 ::DeleteProcThreadAttributeList(attrList);
2076 ::HeapFree(::GetProcessHeap(), 0, attrList);
2077 ::CloseHandle(hNull);
2078 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
2079 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
2080 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2081 QStringLiteral(
2082 "Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'UpdateProcThreadAttribute(HANDLE_LIST)' Error:\n%1")
2083 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
2084 }
2085
2086 // Configure the child standard handles. STDIN comes from the pipe read handle;
2087 // STDOUT and STDERR go to NUL because the helper does not produce output.
2088 STARTUPINFOEXW siex{};
2089 siex.StartupInfo.cb = sizeof(STARTUPINFOEXW);
2090 siex.StartupInfo.dwFlags = STARTF_USESTDHANDLES;
2091 siex.StartupInfo.hStdInput = hRead;
2092 siex.StartupInfo.hStdOutput = hNull;
2093 siex.StartupInfo.hStdError = hNull;
2094 siex.lpAttributeList = attrList;
2095
2096 // Receives the process and main-thread handles created by CreateProcessW().
2097 PROCESS_INFORMATION pi{};
2098
2099 // CreateProcessW may modify the command-line buffer, so pass a mutable copy.
2100 std::wstring mutableCmd = cmdLine;
2101
2102 // Start npiImpLog.exe with no window and with extended startup information.
2103 // bInheritHandles must be TRUE because the handle list controls inheritance.
2104 const BOOL ok = ::CreateProcessW(
2105 impLogExePath.c_str(),
2106 mutableCmd.data(),
2107 nullptr,
2108 nullptr,
2109 TRUE, // must be TRUE when using HANDLE_LIST attribute
2110 CREATE_NO_WINDOW | EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT,
2111 nullptr,
2112 nullptr,
2113 &siex.StartupInfo,
2114 &pi);
2115
2116 // Capture CreateProcessW failure immediately. Cleanup calls may overwrite the
2117 // thread's last-error value.
2118 const DWORD createProcErr = ok ? ERROR_SUCCESS : ::GetLastError();
2119
2120 // The attribute list is needed only during CreateProcessW. After the child is
2121 // created or creation has failed, it can be destroyed and freed.
2122 ::DeleteProcThreadAttributeList(attrList);
2123 ::HeapFree(::GetProcessHeap(), 0, attrList);
2124
2125 if (!ok) {
2126 ::CloseHandle(hNull);
2127 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
2128 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
2129 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2130 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'CreateProcessW' Error:\n%1")
2131 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(createProcErr))));
2132 }
2133
2134 // The parent keeps only the child process handle and the pipe write handle.
2135 // hRead and hNull belong only to the child side after process creation.
2136 ::CloseHandle(hNull);
2137 ::CloseHandle(hRead);
2138 ::CloseHandle(pi.hThread);
2139
2140 // Detect immediate helper startup failure. In normal operation, the helper
2141 // waits on STDIN and this short wait times out.
2142 const DWORD waitResult = ::WaitForSingleObject(pi.hProcess, 250);
2143 if (waitResult == WAIT_FAILED) {
2144 const DWORD err = ::GetLastError();
2145 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2146 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\n'WaitForSingleObject' Error:\n%1")
2147 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err))));
2148 }
2149
2150 // If the helper already exited, treat it as startup failure and report its
2151 // npiImpLog-specific exit code.
2152 if (waitResult == WAIT_OBJECT_0) {
2153 DWORD code = 0;
2154 (void)::GetExitCodeProcess(pi.hProcess, &code);
2155 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2156 QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nStart Imp Log Process Failed.\n\nnpiImpLog.exe returned %1:\n%2")
2157 .arg(static_cast<qulonglong>(code))
2158 .arg(processExitText(code)));
2159 }
2160
2161 // Acquire the pipe lock so that normal messages wait. Then check if
2162 // fatal or crash is not in progress before proceeding to replace the handles.
2163
2164 ::AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_);
2165
2166 HANDLE hProcessOld = leaked.bridge_.hProcess_;
2167 HANDLE hLogPipeOld = leaked.bridge_.hLogPipe_;
2168
2169 const bool crashing =
2170 ::InterlockedCompareExchange(&leaked.crash_.crashing_, 0, 0) != 0;
2171
2172 const bool fatalLog =
2173 leaked.crash_.fatalOwnerThreadId_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0u;
2174
2175 // Acquiring hold is important because fatal and crash messages acquire it before
2176 // sending message to important log process. In case here we are unable to acquire
2177 // hold then it means that fatal or crash is already in progress and there is no
2178 // point in starting the new important log process since the application is going
2179 // to terminate very soon.
2180 if (bool expected = false; crashing || fatalLog || !leaked.bridge_.hold_.compare_exchange_strong(
2181 expected, true, std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
2182 ::ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_);
2183 ::CloseHandle(hWrite);
2184 ::CloseHandle(pi.hProcess);
2185 return;
2186 }
2187
2188 leaked.bridge_.hProcess_ = pi.hProcess;
2189 leaked.bridge_.hLogPipe_ = hWrite;
2190
2191 // Close previous handles
2192
2193 if (hLogPipeOld != nullptr && hLogPipeOld != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
2194 ::CloseHandle(hLogPipeOld);
2195
2196 if (hProcessOld != nullptr && hProcessOld != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
2197 ::CloseHandle(hProcessOld);
2198
2199 // Set the hold to false so that fatal and crash can proceed safely
2200 leaked.bridge_.hold_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
2201
2202 // Release the pipe lock to allow normal messages to go to important log process if needed.
2203 ::ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_);
2204 }
2205
2206 /// \brief Writes a complete byte range to the current important-log pipe.
2207 /// \details Crash-mode calls use bounded lock acquisition and abandon the write
2208 /// rather than risk blocking or recursive failure handling.
2209 void sendData(const char* data, size_t len, bool crash) noexcept
2210 {
2211 LeakedState& leaked = LeakedState::Inst_();
2212
2213 // If crash is true i.e. fatal or crash log, then we acquire hold so that a new
2214 // important log process cannot be started. In other cases pipe lock will be held
2215 // already by either the sendDataLocked or startProcess for synchronization.
2216 bool holdAcquired{false};
2217 if (crash) {
2218 for (int ii = 0; ii < 250; ++ii) {
2219 bool expected = false;
2220 if (leaked.bridge_.hold_.compare_exchange_strong(expected, true, std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
2221 holdAcquired = true;
2222 break;
2223 }
2224 ::YieldProcessor();
2225 }
2226 if (!holdAcquired) return;
2227 }
2228
2229 // Nothing can be written unless the helper process and pipe are valid.
2230 // Invalid input is treated as a no-op because logging must not destabilize
2231 // the caller.
2232 if (leaked.bridge_.hProcess_ == nullptr ||
2233 leaked.bridge_.hLogPipe_ == nullptr ||
2234 leaked.bridge_.hLogPipe_ == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE ||
2235 data == nullptr ||
2236 len == 0) {
2237 if (holdAcquired)
2238 leaked.bridge_.hold_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
2239 return;
2240 }
2241
2242 // Use a byte pointer so pointer arithmetic advances by exact byte count.
2243 // remaining tracks how many bytes still need to be sent to the helper.
2244 const unsigned char* bPtr = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(data);
2245 size_t remaining = len;
2246
2247 // Counts repeated write attempts that made no progress.
2248 // This prevents an infinite loop if the pipe stops accepting data.
2249 int noProgressTries = 0;
2250
2251 while (remaining > 0) {
2252 // WriteFile accepts a DWORD byte count, so very large writes are split into
2253 // DWORD-sized chunks. Normal log writes will usually complete in one chunk.
2254 const size_t chunkSz = (remaining > static_cast<size_t>(0xFFFFFFFFu))
2255 ? static_cast<size_t>(0xFFFFFFFFu)
2256 : remaining;
2257 const DWORD chunk = static_cast<DWORD>(chunkSz);
2258
2259 // Write the current chunk to the pipe connected to npiImpLog.exe STDIN.
2260 // A successful call may still write fewer bytes than requested.
2261 DWORD wrote = 0;
2262 const BOOL ok = ::WriteFile(leaked.bridge_.hLogPipe_, bPtr, chunk, &wrote, nullptr);
2263
2264 if (!ok || wrote == 0) {
2265 // GetLastError is meaningful only when WriteFile fails. If WriteFile
2266 // succeeds but writes zero bytes, use a deterministic synthetic error.
2267 const DWORD err = ok ? ERROR_WRITE_FAULT : ::GetLastError();
2268
2269 // During crash handling, do not show another fatal message or retry deeply.
2270 // Best effort logging is safer than risking recursive failure handling.
2271 if (crash) {
2272 if (holdAcquired)
2273 leaked.bridge_.hold_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
2274 return;
2275 }
2276
2277 // Broken pipe errors mean the helper is gone, so retries are pointless.
2278 // Other no-progress cases are retried briefly before reporting failure.
2279 if (err == ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE || err == ERROR_NO_DATA) {
2280 noProgressTries = 16;
2281 }
2282 else {
2283 ++noProgressTries;
2284 }
2285
2286 // Give transient no-progress cases a few chances. This is intentionally
2287 // short because blocking the main application on logging is worse.
2288 if (noProgressTries < 16) {
2289 ::SwitchToThread();
2290 continue;
2291 }
2292
2293 try {
2294 // Build a diagnostic message containing the pipe write error.
2295 // The helper process state is added below when available.
2296 QString msg = QStringLiteral("WriteFile to npiImpLog pipe failed.");
2297 msg += QStringLiteral("\nGetLastError %1: %2")
2298 .arg(static_cast<qulonglong>(err))
2299 .arg(QString::fromStdWString(npi::ind::winErrorText(err)));
2300
2301 // Broken pipe normally means npiImpLog.exe exited or failed during startup.
2302 // This gives a clearer reason than the raw Win32 error alone.
2303 if (err == ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE || err == ERROR_NO_DATA)
2304 msg += QStringLiteral("\nPipe is closed. The helper likely exited or failed to start.");
2305
2306 // Add helper exit information if the process has already terminated.
2307 // If it is still active, the pipe failure is reported as-is.
2308 DWORD code = STILL_ACTIVE;
2309 if (::GetExitCodeProcess(leaked.bridge_.hProcess_, &code)) {
2310 if (code == STILL_ACTIVE) {
2311 msg += QStringLiteral("\nHelper process is still running.");
2312 }
2313 else {
2314 msg += QStringLiteral("\nHelper exited with code %1: %2")
2315 .arg(static_cast<qulonglong>(code))
2316 .arg(processExitText(code));
2317 }
2318 }
2319
2320 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(QStringLiteral("Fatal Error:\nImp Log Write Failed.\n\n%1").arg(msg));
2321 }
2322 catch (...) {
2323 npi::app::winStopMsgExe(
2324 "Fatal Error:\nImp Log Write Failed.\n\nWriteFile to npiImpLog pipe failed. Diagnostic message construction also failed.");
2325 }
2326 }
2327
2328 // Advance only after confirmed progress. Partial writes are handled by
2329 // continuing the loop with the remaining unwritten bytes.
2330 noProgressTries = 0;
2331 bPtr += wrote;
2332 remaining -= static_cast<size_t>(wrote);
2333 }
2334
2335 if (holdAcquired)
2336 leaked.bridge_.hold_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
2337 }
2338
2339 /// \brief Writes important-log data while coordinating normal, fatal, and crash senders.
2340 /// \details Non-fatal writes hold the pipe lock. Fatal writes try to acquire it and
2341 /// otherwise perform a best-effort unlocked write, so interleaving remains possible.
2342 void sendDataLocked(const char* data, size_t len, bool fatal) noexcept
2343 {
2344 LeakedState& leaked = LeakedState::Inst_();
2345
2346 // In case of fatal logs we try to acquire the pipe lock but proceed
2347 // without it if unable to acquire it. This is the best effort logging
2348 // since it is better to have interleaved data than to not have fatal logs.
2349 if (fatal) {
2350 if (::TryAcquireSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_)) {
2351 sendData(data, len, true);
2352 ::ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_);
2353 }
2354 else {
2355 sendData(data, len, true);
2356 }
2357 return;
2358 }
2359
2360 // For normal non-fatal logs i.e. warning or critical, acquiring the
2361 // pipe lock is a must to avoid interleaving of data.
2362 ::AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_);
2363 sendData(data, len, false);
2364 ::ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&leaked.bridge_.pipeLock_);
2365 }
2366 }
2367
2368 /**
2369 * \brief Installs and implements fatal and abnormal-termination handling.
2370 * \details
2371 * Handlers avoid dynamic allocation where practical, claim a single fatal owner,
2372 * format emergency diagnostics into fixed buffers, forward them to the important
2373 * log helper, and terminate the process without re-entering ordinary logging.
2374 * \note
2375 * Crash handlers intentionally do not show message boxes. They only write a
2376 * small best-effort crash record and then terminate or preserve default crash
2377 * behavior. UI/reporting from these paths should be done by an external process.
2378 */
2379 namespace crash
2380 {
2381 constexpr DWORD fatalOwnerWaitMs = 5000u; ///< Wait time for a fatal/crash log for the first owner to show a popup.
2382
2383 /// \brief Terminates the process immediately without invoking normal cleanup.
2384 [[noreturn]] void hardFailFast() noexcept
2385 {
2386 __fastfail(FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT);
2387 // ReSharper disable once CppUnreachableCode
2388 ::TerminateProcess(::GetCurrentProcess(), 0x40000015u); // STATUS_FATAL_APP_EXIT // NOLINT(clang-diagnostic-unreachable-code)
2389
2390#ifdef _MSC_VER
2391 __assume(0);
2392#endif
2393 }
2394
2395 /// \brief Claims fatal ownership or gives the existing owner a brief reporting period.
2396 /// \details A non-owning thread waits for a fixed grace period and then fails fast.
2397 void claimFatalOwnership(LeakedState::CrashState& crashState, DWORD curThreadId)
2398 {
2399 const std::uint32_t selfThreadId = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(curThreadId);
2400 std::uint32_t expectedThreadId = 0;
2401
2402 if (crashState.fatalOwnerThreadId_.compare_exchange_strong(
2403 expectedThreadId,
2404 selfThreadId,
2405 std::memory_order_acq_rel,
2406 std::memory_order_acquire))
2407 return;
2408
2409 if (expectedThreadId == selfThreadId)
2410 crash::hardFailFast();
2411
2412 ::Sleep(fatalOwnerWaitMs);
2413 crash::hardFailFast();
2414 }
2415
2416 /// \brief Handles an unhandled Windows structured exception.
2417 /// \details The handler formats register and exception information into
2418 /// fixed buffers, forwards the record best-effort, and terminates immediately.
2419 LONG WINAPI windowsExceptionFilter(EXCEPTION_POINTERS* ep) noexcept
2420 {
2421 LeakedState& leaked = LeakedState::Inst_();
2422
2423 if (!ep || !ep->ExceptionRecord)
2424 return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
2425
2426 const DWORD code = ep->ExceptionRecord->ExceptionCode;
2427
2428 if (code == EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT || code == EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP)
2429 return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
2430
2431 if (::InterlockedExchange(&leaked.crash_.crashing_, 1) != 0) {
2432 ::TerminateProcess(::GetCurrentProcess(), static_cast<UINT>(code));
2433 return EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER;
2434 }
2435
2436 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.clear_();
2437
2438 // CASE 1: Stack Overflow (Critical / Low Stack)
2439 if (code == EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW) {
2440 // Best-effort reporting while the faulting thread has very limited stack space.
2441 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_(
2442 "Windows (SEH) Exception: Stack Overflow (Recursion or Stack Exhaustion)");
2443 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.finalizeAsNewLine_();
2444
2445 if (::IsDebuggerPresent())
2446 ::OutputDebugStringA(leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.data_());
2447
2448 bridge::sendData(leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.data_(), leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.size_(), true);
2449
2450 // Kill immediately - we cannot recover safely
2451 ::TerminateProcess(::GetCurrentProcess(), static_cast<UINT>(code));
2452 return EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER;
2453 }
2454
2455 // CASE 2: Standard SEH Crash (Stack is Safe)
2456 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Windows (SEH) Exception: ");
2457
2458 switch (code) {
2459 case EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION:
2460 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Access Violation");
2461 if (ep->ExceptionRecord->NumberParameters >= 1) {
2462 const ULONG_PTR operation = ep->ExceptionRecord->ExceptionInformation[0];
2463
2464 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_(" (");
2465
2466 if (operation == 0) {
2467 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Read");
2468 }
2469 else if (operation == 1) {
2470 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Write");
2471 }
2472 else if (operation == 8) {
2473 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Execute");
2474 }
2475 else {
2476 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Unknown Operation");
2477 }
2478
2479 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_(" Access)");
2480 }
2481 else {
2482 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_(" (Invalid Memory Read/Write/Execute)");
2483 }
2484 break;
2485 case EXCEPTION_ARRAY_BOUNDS_EXCEEDED:
2486 leaked.crash_.crashBuf_.appendRawText_("Array Bounds Exceeded (Bounds-check fault)");
2487 break;
2488 case EXCEPTION_FLT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO:
